newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Lili closes in on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili closes in on Cuba.

text.p: Hurricane Lili closed in on Cuba Thursday, threatening the island with torrential rains and flooding, the National Hurricane Center said.
Forecasters said the forward motion of the storm, a minimal hurricane with winds of 75 mph (120 kph), could slow in the next 24 hours.

At 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT), the center of Lili was located at latitude 20.4 north, longitude 83.1 west, about 185 miles (300 km) south-southwest of Havana, and was moving to the north-northeast at about 9 mph (15 kph).
A hurricane warning issued by the Cuban government was in effect for the Isle of Youth and the mainland from Camaguey province westward, the hurricane center said.
A tropical storm warning and hurricane watch remained in effect for the Cayman Islands. Forecasters said alerts could be issued for the Florida Keys and parts of the Bahamas later Thursday.
On its current track, the center of Lili was expected to approach the south Cuba coast late Thursday or early Friday.
Hurricane-force winds extended 25 miles (40 km) from the center and tropical storm-force winds extended outward up to 140 miles (220 km).
Rainfall up to 12 inches (30 cm) was likely over Cuba, the Cayman Islands and parts of Central America, raising the possibility of life-threatening flash floods and mud slides in mountainous areas.
Storm surge flooding of three to six feet (1-2 meters) was possible near where the storm crosses mainland Cuba, forecasters said.
Rainbands from the storm were spreading over the islands and into the Florida Straits. Forecasters warned boaters in the Florida Keys to remain in port.
